title: Matrix multiplication: schoolbook vs Strassen
problem_statement: Given two n x n matrices A and B over the integers, compute C = AB.

input.size_measure: 2n^2 entries (small integers in the harness, so arithmetic is unit cost).

algorithms.name: schoolbook
algorithms.pseudocode: for i, j: C[i][j] = sum over k of A[i][k] * B[k][j]

algorithms.name: Strassen
algorithms.idea: Split each matrix into 2 x 2 blocks; seven block products (instead of eight) plus additions suffice. Recurse.
algorithms.pseudocode: see implementation (the seven products M1..M7 and their combinations are written out in PROOFS.md section 4)
algorithms.correctness: Strassen 1969: the seven products combine to the four blocks of C by a direct algebraic identity that never commutes two factors, so it is valid over any ring, in particular over the ring of half-size integer matrices; induction over the recursion and the zero padding give AB (PROOFS.md section 4, with a symbolic check of the code). T(n) = 7T(n/2) + Theta(n^2) gives Theta(n^log2(7)) (PROOFS.md section 5).

shape.note: starts at the schoolbook cutoff (16); 6 terms, so the holdout is lowered to 2 (n = 1024 would cost about 7 times n = 512)

relationship: Both polynomial; Strassen lowers the exponent from 3 to log2(7) ~ 2.807. The later exponent bounds (Coppersmith-Winograd, ..., Alman et al.) and AlphaTensor's rank-47 scheme for 4 x 4 matrices over GF(2) are background (see background). Applied recursively, a scheme with r > k^2 products for k x k matrices gives omega <= log_k(r) over every field in which it is valid (PROOFS.md section 8). If a rank-47 bilinear scheme for <4,4,4> over GF(2) exists (background: Fawzi et al. 2022, Fig. 3), then omega <= log4(47) ~ 2.7773 in characteristic 2. Two levels of Strassen's algorithm use 7^2 = 49 multiplications for 4 x 4 matrices (PROOFS.md section 8).

background.statement: Coppersmith and Winograd give a matrix multiplication algorithm via arithmetic progressions (title); its exponent bound is not stated or checked here.

Alman, Duan, Vassilevska Williams, Xu, Xu and Zhou show omega < 2.371339 in versions 1 and 2 (SODA 2025) of arXiv:2404.16349; version 3 of the same record (2026-08-19) states omega < 2.371177. The line of improvements between Coppersmith-Winograd and these bounds is not listed here.
background.source: Alman et al. 2024, arXiv:2404.16349, abstracts of versions 1 and 2 (SODA 2025) and of version 3 (2026-08-19)

background.statement: AlphaTensor found a scheme that multiplies 4 x 4 matrices with 47 multiplications in modular arithmetic (Z_2).
background.source: Fawzi et al. 2022, main text and Fig. 3

sources.authors: Alman, J.; Duan, R.; Vassilevska Williams, V.; Xu, Y.; Xu, Z.; Zhou, R.
sources.title: More Asymmetry Yields Faster Matrix Multiplication

sources.authors: Fawzi, A.; Balog, M.; Huang, A.; et al.
sources.title: Discovering faster matrix multiplication algorithms with reinforcement learning

verification.method: V1: both implementations agree on random integer matrices for n = 0..10 and n = 17, 31, 40, 64 (above the recursion cutoff of 16) and pass an independent exact check that recomputes every entry of A·B. V2 (since 2026-10-06, RESEARCH_LOG RL-047): the measured quantity is the exact number of SCALAR MULTIPLICATIONS performed by the unchanged implementations, counted by an instrumented number type in the harness, which counts a product when at least one operand is instrumented. For n not a power of two the matrices are padded with plain zeros, and products whose two operands both come from padding zeros alone are not counted (n = 17, padded to 32: 24832 counted of the 28672 performed); the V2 sizes are powers of two, where no padding occurs. On n = 32, 64, 128, 256: schoolbook = n^3 exactly; Strassen = 7^(log2(n/16)) * 16^3 exactly (this closed form holds for every n = 16 * 2^k). Each claim is fitted with tolerance 0.02 (the counts are exact, so no timing noise) and the other algorithm's cost is a declared rival that must NOT fit: alpha of Strassen's counts against n^3 is log2(7)/3 = 0.936, of the schoolbook counts against n^log2(7) is 3/log2(7) = 1.069, both outside the band. Wall-clock timing remains unable to separate the two (RL-006); additions are not counted. Proofs: PROOFS.md proves every claim of this entry from the code (the correctness of both algorithms, including Strassen's identities, the recursion and the padding; the time and space bounds; the exact multiplication counts for all sizes of their domains and the exact addition counts; the value sizes; the step from a fixed-size scheme to an exponent bound) and names the scripts and tests that check each one, among them tests/test_proofs_strassen.py.

caveats: The algorithms behind the exponent bounds in the background are not implemented or verified in this entry. Over the integers all arithmetic of both methods is exact (PROOFS.md section 9).
notes: AlphaTensor improvements are for fixed small block sizes; only when such a scheme is applied recursively does it become an asymptotic (T3) statement.
